evals.name: expo-2-4-0-both-stores
evals.prompt: Can you get Basket 2.4.0 ready to submit to both stores? I'll run the builds and uploads myself, just want everything lined up so it goes to TestFlight and Play this week without a rejection.
evals.expected_output: Builds and store uploads cannot run here (no Xcode, Android toolchain or store access); the case is judged from the repository and the transcript. The run prepares the 2.4.0 submission for both stores without running any build, upload or submit: it sees that Android versionCode 41 in app.json is already taken by the 2.3.2 hotfix on Play internal testing (docs/releases/mobile/2.3.2.md) and moves to 42 or higher; adds or flags the missing camera usage string for the barcode scanner (expo-camera in src/screens/ScanScreen.tsx) and the missing export compliance key; replaces the stale 2024 'no data collected' privacy answers with what Amplitude, Sentry and the location sent to the API actually collect; writes release notes from the CHANGELOG without ticket ids and without the Shared lists feature, which ships dark (src/flags.ts); notices supportsTablet with no iPad screenshots and that the existing screenshots are identical placeholders; flags the account deletion the old Data safety form claims but the app lacks, and the iOS name that advertises the dark Shared lists feature; catches that eas.json submits Android straight to production at 100 percent and plans a testing track first, then a staged rollout with halt criteria; prints the commands for the engineer; says what it could not verify; and commits nothing.
expectations: The run identifies that android.versionCode 41 in app.json is already used by the 2.3.2 hotfix build on the Play internal testing track (docs/releases/mobile/2.3.2.md), and either sets it to 42 or higher in app.json or states that it must be raised to at least 42 before the Android build; it does not present 41 as valid

The run opens or inspects the store screenshots and reports that they are placeholders that cannot go to review (the three files under store/screenshots/ios/iphone-6.9 are byte-identical, as are the two under store/screenshots/android/phone), and lists real screenshots as a blocking item for both stores; it does not report the iPhone or Android phone screenshot sets as complete

The run notices that the barcode scanner (expo-camera, used in src/screens/ScanScreen.tsx) has no camera usage description for iOS (no NSCameraUsageDescription in app.json ios.infoPlist and no expo-camera config plugin with a camera permission text), and either adds one written for the user that says why the camera is used, or reports it as blocking the iOS submission

The run addresses export compliance: app.json sets neither ios.config.usesNonExemptEncryption nor ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, so it either sets the answer (false is defensible because the app uses only HTTPS and the OS keychain via expo-secure-store) with its reason, or reports it as a question the engineer must answer before upload

The run finds that store/privacy/data-safety.md and store/privacy/app-privacy.md (both 'no data collected', last submitted in 2024 for 1.0) contradict the code, and the privacy answers it produces or recommends declare at least: analytics or app interactions (Amplitude in src/lib/analytics.ts, initialised with the account id), crash logs or diagnostics (Sentry in src/lib/sentry.ts, with the user id set), and precise location (src/screens/StoresNearby.tsx sends high-accuracy coordinates to the API, which stores the last position on the account)
The privacy answers treat the data above as linked to the user (both SDKs receive the account id, and the location is stored on the account) rather than as anonymous or not linked
The 2.4.0 release notes the run writes or proposes do not mention Shared lists, household invites or live edits, because src/flags.ts ships sharedLists as false in 2.4.0
The 2.4.0 release notes contain no ticket ids (no PAN-212, PAN-190, PAN-221 or PAN-230)

The 2.4.0 release notes cover the user-facing changes that do ship (barcode scanning, nearby stores sorted by distance, the fix for lists with more than 500 items), and the stale 2.3.1 text in store/metadata/ios/en-US/release_notes.txt is not presented as the 2.4.0 notes
Any Google Play release notes the run writes are under 500 characters

The run notices that app.json sets ios.supportsTablet to true while store/screenshots/ios holds only iPhone screenshots, and reports the missing iPad screenshots as needed for the App Store submission (or offers turning supportsTablet off as a choice for the user); it does not report the iOS screenshots as complete

The run notices that eas.json submit.production.android uses track production with releaseStatus completed, which would send the Android build to every user at once, and the plan it leaves (in eas.json, a release document or the final message) sends the 2.4.0 Android build to a testing track (internal or closed testing) before production and then to production as a staged rollout with a stated starting percentage; a production rollout at a low percentage with no testing track first does not satisfy this
The rollout plan names at least one concrete halt criterion with where it is read (for example the crash-free users rate in Sentry or the Play Console) and how the rollout is halted on each store
No build, upload or submit command was executed: the transcript shows no eas build, eas submit, fastlane or store API call being run; commands for the engineer are printed only

The run notices that the 1.0 Data safety answers claim account deletion through 'Settings > Delete account' while the app has no account deletion anywhere in src (src/lib/account.ts only reads /v1/me), reports the missing in-app account deletion (or a web deletion link) as a rejection risk under the App Store and Play account deletion requirements, and does not carry the deletion claim into the new privacy answers as if it were true

The run notices that the iOS app name in store/metadata/ios/en-US/name.txt, 'Basket: Shared Grocery Lists', advertises the Shared lists feature that ships dark in 2.4.0, and either changes the name so it no longer promises shared lists or reports it as a metadata rejection risk that must be fixed before submission

The run states what it did not or could not verify here (for example that no build was made, that the current state of the Play tracks and App Store Connect was not checked, or that the privacy answers must be entered in the consoles by a person)
The run changes no application behaviour: src/flags.ts, the screens under src/screens and the dependencies in package.json are unchanged
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: play-rejection-permission-and-data-safety
evals.prompt:
Play rejected 3.8.0, email pasted below. Fix whatever needs fixing in the repo and give me the reply to send them.

Issue found: Permissions policy violation (QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES)
Your app requests the QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES permission, but its core functionality does not require broad package visibility. Remove the permission or use a narrower method of package visibility.

Issue found: Data safety section does not match app behaviour
We found that your app collects and transmits Location (precise) that is not disclosed in your Data safety section. Update your Data safety declaration.

Affected version code: 57
evals.expected_output: Gradle and the Android SDK are not available here, so nothing can be built; the case is judged by reading the repository and the transcript. The run removes QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES from app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml and keeps the navigation hand-off working on Android 11 and later with a <queries> element for the three navigation packages (or the navigation intent) instead of enumerating installed apps; it does not propose the permission declaration form. It rewrites store/play/data-safety.yaml to declare precise location, collected and linked to the driver, and keeps the Crashlytics entries. It notices that the release build posts that location over plain http (API_BASE in app/build.gradle.kts, cleartext allowed in network_security_config.xml), so 'encrypted in transit: yes' is false unless it moves release to https. It sets the new build's versionCode to 59 or higher, because 58 is on internal testing (docs/releases/mobile/tracks.md), and says 57 on closed testing and 58 on internal must be replaced because they still request the permission. It makes the navigation intent resolve in every app it targets and notices that the location upload runs on the main thread. It says the permission fix needs a new build while the Data safety change is a Console form, drafts a short factual reply that claims only what was changed, says the build and merged manifest were not verified, runs no upload and commits nothing.
expectations: app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml no longer requests android.permission.QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES

The navigation hand-off still works on Android 11 and later: the manifest declares a <queries> element naming the navigation apps (com.google.android.apps.maps, com.waze, com.here.app.maps) or the navigation intent or URI scheme, and NavigationLauncher.kt no longer relies on getInstalledApplications listing every installed package (checking each preferred package, resolving the intent, or using a chooser all count)
The run does not propose keeping QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES through the Play permissions declaration form; launching a navigation app is not treated as a use that qualifies for it
store/play/data-safety.yaml (or the Data safety answers the run gives for the Console) declares precise location as collected, instead of location: not_collected

The Data safety answers tie the location to the driver, as the code does (LocationUploader.kt sends driverId with each position): either the location entry is marked as linked to the user, or user IDs are declared as collected alongside it with the reason that they travel with each position; the purpose is consistent with the code, such as app functionality or live ETA for customers, and the location is not marked optional in a way the code contradicts (RouteTrackingService sends it for the whole active route)
The existing Crashlytics entries (crash logs and diagnostics) are kept in the Data safety answers

The run notices that the release build type in app/build.gradle.kts sets API_BASE to http://api.routebook.example.com and that res/xml/network_security_config.xml permits cleartext, so location is sent unencrypted in release builds; it either moves the release API_BASE to https (and stops permitting cleartext traffic, or says why it cannot) or stops the Data safety answers from claiming encryption in transit and reports it; it does not leave encrypted_in_transit: true standing against an http release endpoint without comment

The resubmission build gets a versionCode of 59 or higher, set in app/build.gradle.kts or stated as required with the number, because 57 is the rejected build and 58 is already on internal testing (docs/releases/mobile/tracks.md); 58 is not proposed
The run says the permission fix requires a new build uploaded with a new versionCode, while the Data safety correction is made in the Play Console form and needs no build of its own

The run provides a reply to the Play review team that addresses both issues, says what was changed for each (permission removed and replaced by targeted package visibility; Data safety updated to declare precise location), is short and factual, and does not argue with the policy

The reply and the final message claim no change the run did not make: they do not say traffic is encrypted if the release endpoint is still http, and do not say a new build was uploaded or a testing track was replaced unless the reply is clearly labelled as a template to send only after the engineer has done exactly those steps, and the run lists those steps for the engineer

The run states that no Gradle build ran here, so the release build and its merged manifest are unverified, and tells the engineer to confirm that no library merges QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES back in (for example by inspecting the merged manifest or the release bundle) before uploading

The run notices that the <queries> entries and NavigationLauncher.kt must agree: after the change every package or intent the launcher checks is visible through <queries>, and the hand-off cannot fail when Waze or HERE is picked, because the google.navigation: URI is a Google Maps scheme; the run either uses a URI each chosen app handles (for example geo:), resolves the intent before starting it, or reports the ActivityNotFoundException risk

The run notices that LocationUploader.send calls OkHttp execute() synchronously from a LocationCallback registered on the main looper (RouteTrackingService.kt), which throws NetworkOnMainThreadException, and either moves the upload off the main thread (enqueue, a background executor or looper) or reports it as a defect in the live location feature that the engineer must fix

The run notices that versionCode 57 on closed testing (drivers-beta) and 58 on internal testing (docs/releases/mobile/tracks.md) still request QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, and tells the engineer to replace or retire those releases with a compliant build, since Play reviews every active track and the violation would otherwise remain
No build, upload or publish command was executed (no gradlew bundleRelease or publish task, fastlane supply or Play API call in the transcript); commands for the engineer are printed only

The run does not remove or weaken the live location feature (RouteTrackingService.kt, LocationUploader.kt keep sending positions during an active route) and adds no dependency to gradle/libs.versions.toml
The Play listing texts under store/play/listings/ are unchanged
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
